person.name: Henry_II
person.summary: Henry II (6 May 973 – 13 July 1024), also known as Saint Henry, was Duke of Bavaria (from 995, as Henry IV), elected King of the Romans in 1002, anointed King of Italy in 1004, and crowned Holy Roman Emperor by Pope Benedict VIII in 1014. The last ruler of the Ottonian line, he strengthened imperial authority through close cooperation with the Church, founded the Diocese of Bamberg, campaigned against Bolesław I of Poland, intervened in Bohemia, and led multiple expeditions into Italy before dying childless in 1024.

events.title: Moves to secure the regalia after Otto III’s death
events.description: Following Emperor Otto III’s death, Henry confronted the funeral procession at Polling seeking the Imperial Regalia, detained Archbishop Heribert of Cologne when rebuffed, and failed to win election at Aachen, setting the stage for a disputed succession.

events.title: Crowned King of Germany (Rex Romanorum)
events.description: Henry was anointed and crowned King of Germany at Mainz by Archbishop Willigis, adopting the title Rex Romanorum and asserting his rule despite initial opposition.

events.title: Cunigunde crowned Queen of Germany
events.description: Archbishop Willigis crowned Cunigunde of Luxembourg as Queen of Germany at Paderborn, consolidating Henry’s new royal household.

location_coordinates.label: Paderborn, Kreis Paderborn, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany
location_coordinates.name: Paderborn, Kingdom of Germany

events.title: Revolt of Henry of Schweinfurt and reorganization in Bavaria
events.description: After Henry II refused to grant him Bavaria, Margrave Henry of Schweinfurt rebelled with Polish support. The revolt was crushed; the margrave was deposed and the March of Nordgau abolished, with its secular authority transferred to the new Diocese of Bamberg.

location_coordinates.label: Weißenburg in Bayern, Weißenburg-Gunzenhausen, Bavaria, 91781, Germany
location_coordinates.name: Nordgau (Bavaria), Kingdom of Germany

events.title: Anointed King of Italy
events.description: Henry entered Italy to confront Arduin of Ivrea and was anointed King of Italy at Pavia, restoring German royal authority south of the Alps.

events.title: Intervention in Bohemia against Polish control
events.description: Henry supported Duke Jaromír of Bohemia against Polish domination, bringing Bohemia effectively within the framework of the Holy Roman Empire.

location_coordinates.label: Bohemia, Town of Islip, Suffolk County, New York, 11716, United States
location_coordinates.name: Bohemia (Prague), Holy Roman Empire

events.title: Founding of the Diocese of Bamberg
events.description: To strengthen ecclesiastical administration and royal authority, Henry established the Diocese of Bamberg, endowing it with former Nordgau territories.

events.title: Crowned Holy Roman Emperor by Pope Benedict VIII
events.description: In Rome, Pope Benedict VIII crowned Henry as Holy Roman Emperor, formalizing his imperial authority over the Empire.

events.title: Peace of Bautzen with Bolesław I of Poland
events.description: After years of conflict, Henry concluded the Peace of Bautzen with Bolesław I the Brave, stabilizing the Empire’s eastern frontier.

events.title: Final Italian expedition against Byzantine influence
events.description: Henry led a southern Italian campaign to curb Byzantine advances and assert imperial suzerainty, operating in regions such as Apulia and Campania.

location_coordinates.label: El Rincón de Capua, Calle Capua, Los Campos, El Centro, Gijón / Xixón, Gijón, Asturias, 33202, Spain
location_coordinates.name: Capua, Principality of Capua

events.title: Death of Henry II
events.description: Henry II died without an heir, ending the Ottonian dynasty; the German princes subsequently elected Conrad II as his successor.

location_coordinates.name: Grona (near Göttingen), Duchy of Saxony
